feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce clarity and polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools add credibility.  
- Broad yet coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are aligned to the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to sharpen structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: standardize punctuation in bullet lists, hyphenation, and serial commas. Examples: “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”; “organization-wide”/“member-facing” are good, but maintain this style throughout. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that clearly positions you as a senior public-sector digital leader. It would be sharper with a more distinctive value proposition and fewer broad phrases that repeat elsewhere in the CV.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground scale/enterprise scope: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading enterprise platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more executive language such as “leading modernization of” or “shaping.”
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent work, such as large-scale web modernization, analytics ecosystems, or AI-enabled search.
- Consider revised version: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives web modernization, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes later skills sections; streamline to avoid repetition.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use slightly shorter, sharper phrases and keep the list consistently scoped to strategic competencies.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel digital communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences” for clearer specificity.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled” already appear in the header.
- Several items also repeat Topline Skills categories; consider using this section for broader themes and leaving tools/platforms to later sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and simplify phrasing: e.g., “Created an AI-powered legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; “10×20-foot” is fine, but keep all items in the same sentence structure.
- Where possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale marker to differentiate these from general responsibilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work closely overlap with Work Experience bullets; this section should emphasize standout deliverables or outcomes rather than restating duties.
- “Editorial storytelling” and “production and distribution” echo existing experience language; consider more project-specific details.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and cross-channel communications governance.”
- Convert duties into 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; e.g. “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components, including downloadable member toolkits, to support advocacy and member engagement.”
- Combine overlapping technical items: merge “CMS development, front-end implementation and troubleshooting” into one concise bullet tied to public-facing site performance, reliability, or launch support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, or workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance… across web, email, social and multimedia” repeat themes already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role.
- The microsite and AI-enabled search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/enterprise scope, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, % improvements, production volume, reporting adoption, or efficiency gains from governance/analytics changes.
- Consolidate channel language: combine email/social into one concise bullet and focus on strategic reach or engagement rather than listing platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer project examples; keep the CV item focused on organizational capability created.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the more senior Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it around executional leadership, recurring outputs, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Make bullets more action/result-focused: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent digital production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating “built/expanded video” too heavily since video growth also appears in the 2015–2018 role and the recent projects section.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:  
  Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance & content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- If space allows, align one phrase to recent impact, e.g. “Enterprise web and content modernization” instead of the broader “digital strategy.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “governance,” “operations,” and “strategy” since those recur credibly in 2022–present experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already well covered in Work Experience; avoid repeating it elsewhere unless differentiated.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too broad and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline skills line, tighten it to the most market-relevant, recent strengths and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint & Power Pages • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization since that is most supported by recent NACo work; move lower-value or older tools later.
- Replace the simple platform list with grouped capability phrasing to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, consider “Enterprise Drupal platforms” instead of just “Drupal” to better match the 10,000+ page migration story.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; keep them here only if you want this section to skew more technical.
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery, and API integrations are repeated in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization, not just tool names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing language: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “performance and search optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework development, executive reporting dashboards, and performance optimization using GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity, and SEO analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this version more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting dashboards” and overlaps with prior work-experience bullets unless made more outcome-oriented.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value operational leadership and event delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task-level to capability-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio and control-room operations,” “PTZ camera systems.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio operations and PTZ camera systems”
- If space allows, add scale/context tied to recent work: “in-house studio buildout” or “advocacy and event programming” to connect with the Director role.
- Drop “video editing” unless editing is a target-role requirement; it feels more junior than the leadership profile.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording here.
- Tool-level detail also appears in Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows”), so keep this section focused on strategic capabilities, not software/process duplication.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strategic relevance and recency: **Drupal • SharePoint • Power Pages • WordPress • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • SharePoint & Power Pages (Microsoft ecosystem) • WordPress • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, replace GitHub Pages with a stronger platform/tool only if used materially in recent roles; otherwise keep it last.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or making one more detailed and the other more selective.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent experience, so avoid overemphasizing it in multiple sections without adding new context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value.
- Group related items for readability: front-end languages, integration/deployment, and edge/performance tooling.
- If accurate, consider replacing one generic item with a stronger implementation signal tied to recent work, e.g. “Drupal front-end implementation” or “CI/CD for web deployments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing in both places.
- GTM may also fit under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if you need space here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of systems leadership. Given the rest of the CV, emphasize automation/build systems and trim lower-value collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/impact: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop **Basecamp** unless used recently or materially; it feels older/less central than the others.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello (project workflows) • Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Collaboration tools like Slack/Teams are lower-signal than automation platforms; keep them only if this section needs breadth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement leadership. Given the strong recent NACo email work, this item should better signal enterprise-scale communications systems and audience engagement.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: **Higher Logic (enterprise/member communications)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/segmentation)** • **Mailchimp (campaign execution)**
- If space allows, tie to outcomes-oriented capability rather than just tools: **newsletter operations, segmentation, automation, and member engagement campaigns**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets already covering email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating audience scale here unless you add a distinct systems angle.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize optimization capability, not just software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • dashboard development • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Put the strongest, most strategic tools first: lead with **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI** to match the most recent experience.
- Replace generic **Dashboarding** with **dashboard development** or **executive reporting** for sharper phrasing; if true, consider **conversion analysis** or **behavior analysis** instead of one broad term.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider consolidating or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same sequence elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/audience for weekly videos, or workflow gains (faster publishing, better coordination, increased output).
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily production work of a digital media associate.”
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and mentored a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo entries; specify what changed or cut it here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation/program support plus the podcast as a concrete first.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Tighten generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” into clearer ownership: “produced digital and multimedia content” or “developed multimedia materials for program and policy communications.”
- Add scope or output if available: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.
- Possible rewrite: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities. Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications and launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production, and rollout.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia language already covered in later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/research support.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
- Rewrite as: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream studio production**
